description: Intent-fulfilment cases (spec 23 §Evaluation) built from THIS repository's own history. The stated intent of a pre-written case is a verbatim slice of a `specs/*.md` section as it existed at a commit that is a strict ancestor of the change under test: a document approved before the implementation existed, written in the register a real ticket is, several sections of which contain clauses the project genuinely never implemented. The post-hoc arm judges the SAME diffs against each change's own commit message, and exists only to isolate intent provenance from case difficulty; the two arms are reported separately and never pooled. Every expectation is the fixed human enumeration of what a human read in the excerpt and found genuinely not done at head - never an engine's output, and never extended because a run surfaced something new. No case is synthetic: nothing was removed from, added to, or reworded in any excerpt to manufacture a leftover. Hydration is local git only: every commit named here is in this repository's history, so the corpus needs no network and spends nothing to materialise.

curation.note: Transcribed from the surviving instrument at `.codereviewer/eval/intent-corpus-realistic/`, which is gitignored and could not be reproduced from a clean checkout. Its case definitions and its fixed human enumeration are committed here; its PER-OBLIGATION hand labels are not, because those were written against engine-produced statements joined by positional obligation id and cannot be carried to a fresh run. The 21 pre-written cases were built from 13 commits across specs 05/11/13/15/19/20/21/22/23/24/25.

rejections.reason: They label statements an extraction produced, addressed by positional id (`obl_1`..`obl_N` in report order), which do not survive a re-run. Committing them would either fix the answer key to one stored round or require matching a hand label onto a statement a human never read - and the statements themselves are engine output, which this project forbids as a source of ground truth.

Its own README records that obligations extracted from a commit message are addressed by construction, and that three rounds of measurement found ZERO genuinely-unaddressed obligations in its real arm. Its diffs survive here as the post-hoc control arm; its cases do not.

rejections.candidate: `pw08-spec15-signals` item 5 - "no EvidenceRecord is produced by a security detection"
rejections.reason: It shares a source line with item 4 ("no security support signal is emitted"): one sentence asks for both, and no sentence boundary separates them. Anchors must partition the excerpt so one reported obligation cannot answer for two rows, so the less specific of the pair is left out rather than given an invented boundary.

rejections.candidate: `pw10-spec15-accept` item 2 - "the acceptance bar 'before any detector ships' is breached"
rejections.reason: It is a statement about the same acceptance clause item 1 already anchors, not a second clause. Splitting one bullet across two rows would double-count a single reported obligation.
